judged_text: Both 'valid host' tests stub retrieved_recently? directly ('topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false)' / '.returns(true)'), so the redis throttle logic introduced in this diff ($redis.setnx on 'retrieved:<url>' plus $redis.expire(key, 60), lines 20-29 of lib/topic_retriever.rb) is never executed by any test. The real throttle code is only covered by mocks of itself: a regression where setnx succeeds but expire is never called (leaving a permanent key that throttles the URL forever after the first retrieval), or where the no_throttle branch (user.try(:staff?) from Jobs::RetrieveTopic) is inverted, passes the suite; only the one-line short-circuit 'perform_retrieve unless (invalid_host? || retrieved_recently?)' is actually verified.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the “valid host” examples stub `retrieved_recently?` directly (`topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false/true)`), so the actual redis-throttle implementation in lib/topic_retriever.rb (`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` inside `retrieved_recently?`) is never executed by tests. As a result, regressions in the throttle logic (including forgetting to call `expire`) or the `no_throttle` branch (used by Jobs::RetrieveTopic when `user.try(:staff?)`) would not be caught. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven runtime defect.
